newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Survivor says he walked out of Guam crashed jet.
newsitem.headline: Survivor says he walked out of Guam crashed jet.

text.p: A South Korean survivor said he pulled a woman from a crashed Korean Air Lines (KAL) jumbo jet before he walked out of the wreckage on Wednesday but fire stopped him from rescuing trapped children.
"As I tried to get out of the plane in a hurry, fearing possible explosions, a lady pulled my foot," Hong Hyon-song said in a telephone interview with state television Korea Broadcasting System.
Hong, 35, said he was one of the first to escape the inferno after the Boeing 747-300, with 231 passengers and 23 crew, crashed in hilly jungle on the Pacific island of Guam.
"It was dark but I could figure that a lady was there. I pulled her arms and got out by clearing leaves around. I was worried the plane might explode," he said.
Some witnesses said the crash impact split the aircraft into five parts.
Hong said the split made an opening right above his seat in row three. "I was lucky. I only had some bruises on my chest. Otherwise I'm fine."
He said he and the woman, who was badly burned, had to wait in darkness for about an hour before being rescued.
He said he set fire to clothes and waved at a military helicopter to catch rescuers' attention.
"The lady was badly injured so the rescuers had to go back to get stretchers. I walked up the hill and was flown to hospital by helicopter," he added.
Hong said an injured female flight attendant asked her to return to the wreckage to help others out.
"When I shouted into the wreckage asking whether anybody was alive, children shouted for help. I asked them 'how many' and they said 'four'.
"It was frustrating and unfortunate but I could not get back in because fire caused blasts inside the plane," he said.

Andrew Murphy, spokesman for the Guam Airport Authority, said 35 survivors were taken to hospital. Guam Governor Carl Gutierrez said more than 200 of the 254 people on board the flight 801 died in the crash.
Hong said he was not warned of any trouble during the approach to the landing.
"I certainly felt landing gears were lowered. I thought the plane was skidding off the runway to the grass nearby. But when I looked out I saw trees passing past windows.
"Then suddenly there was a bang and the plane hit into the ground," he said.
